## starci check

select existing runtime and app checks by test ladder level

### starci check run

run changed-scope checks or the full structural check set

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--level` | enum L0|L1|L2|L3|L4 (default L1) |  |
| `--changed` | list |  |

Effect: read

Roles: worker, lead, coordinator, release, owner

Conventions:

- Use L1 while working, L2 before asking for a land, and L3 when an IO slot changed.
- Runtime L1 selects only manifest self-checks whose implementation path changed; L2 and above run the full check.
- App L1 uses starci app check --fast; L2 and above use the full app check, with every example added at L4.

exit: 0 every selected check passed; 1 check findings; 2 usage or ladder policy refusal

json: starci/check-run@1

```sh
starci check run --level L1 --changed scripts/checks/check-doc-language.mjs
starci check run --level L2
```

## starci docker

build and run application-owned Docker resources without crossing project boundaries

### starci docker build

build one declared application image from the application root

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--tag` | string (default dev) |  |
| `--no-cache` | boolean |  |

Positionals: app

Effect: host

Roles: worker, lead, coordinator, owner

Conventions:

- build context is the app root and the Dockerfile is be/apps/<app>/Dockerfile or fe/apps/<app>/Dockerfile
- the local tag is <project>/<app>:<tag>; this verb never pushes and never logs in
- published ports come from the project's 41000-44999 block
- never touch containers of another project (the protected local installation) or ports 3000 and 3100
- clean up with `starci docker down`

exit: 0 the image was built; 1 Docker build failed; 2 usage or Docker ownership policy was refused

json: starci/docker-build@1

```sh
starci docker build identity
starci docker build landing --tag dev --no-cache --json
```

### starci docker down

remove only the labelled resources owned by one application stack

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--env` | string (default dev) |  |
| `--volumes` | boolean |  |

Positionals: stack

Effect: host

Roles: worker, lead, coordinator, owner

Conventions:

- containers and networks are selected by starci.project and the exact Compose project label, never by a name pattern
- --volumes removes only volumes carrying both ownership labels and never runs docker system prune
- published ports come from the project's 41000-44999 block
- never touch containers of another project (the protected local installation) or ports 3000 and 3100
- clean up with `starci docker down`

exit: 0 selected resources were removed; 1 Docker failed; 2 usage or Docker ownership policy was refused

starci docker down api --volumes --json

| flag | type | |

Effect: read

- --all may show a protected foreign container tagged foreign but never grants authority to mutate it

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--env` | string (default dev) |  |
| `--wait-seconds` | number (default 120) |  |

Positionals: stack

Effect: host

Roles: worker, lead, coordinator, owner

Conventions:

- published ports come from the project's 41000-44999 block and never use 3000, 3100, 54320-54329 or 55321-55327

## starci git

commit, sync, land and back up work through the conventions of the source process

### starci git backup

push local branch tips only to dated backup refs

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--remote` | string (default origin) |  |
| `--branches` | list |  |
| `--dry-run` | boolean |  |

Effect: remote

Roles: coordinator, owner

Conventions:

- backup writes only refs/backup/<yyyy-mm-dd>/<branch>, never branches or tags
- backup refs trigger no workflow and are the only push a coordinator may make
- pushes are never forced and the pre-push hook is never bypassed

exit: 0 backup refs pushed or the dry run is valid; 1 the push failed; 2 invalid remote, branch or force request

json: starci/git-backup@1

```sh
starci git backup
starci git backup --branches lane/cli --branches main --dry-run
```

### starci git commit

commit staged work with the message convention and trailers

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--type` | enum feat|fix|refactor|test|docs|chore|land|release | required |
| `--scope` | string |  |
| `--summary` | string | required |
| `--body` | string |  |
| `--paths` | list |  |
| `--lane` | string |  |
| `--co-author` | string |  |
| `--dry-run` | boolean |  |

Effect: local-write

Roles: lead, coordinator, release, owner

Conventions:

- subjects use `type(scope): summary`; types are feat, fix, refactor, test, docs, chore, land and release
- keep one logical change in each commit and pass explicit paths instead of staging unrelated work
- hooks run the L0 checks; never bypass them and never amend a pushed or landed commit

exit: 0 committed or the dry run is valid; 1 nothing to commit or Git failed; 2 invalid message, path or branch policy

json: starci/git-commit@1

```sh
starci git commit --type fix --scope cli --summary "handle an empty index"
starci git commit --type docs --summary "explain backup refs" --paths docs/git-governance.md --dry-run
```

### starci git land

verify a lane and fast-forward it onto local main without pushing

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--verified` | string |  |
| `--verified-log` | string |  |
| `--dry-run` | boolean |  |
| `--lane` | string |  |
| `--kernel-note` | string |  |
| `--concurrency` | number (default 4) |  |

Positionals: worktree, ref

Effect: local-write

Roles: coordinator, owner

Conventions:

- land only after starci test run --level L2 --against <ref> is green
- lands are serial and hold the host land lock through the gate, check, specs and local merge
- local main is the only destination; a land never pushes, tags or touches origin
- delta lands use --verified with the matching --verified-log and always rerun prior-red spec files

exit: 0 the verification passed and local main fast-forwarded, or a dry run passed without moving it; 1 refused at a named gate, check, spec, lock or fast-forward step; 2 bad usage

json: starci/git-land@1

```sh
starci git land <worktree> <ref>
starci git land <worktree> <ref> --verified <sha> --verified-log <file> --concurrency 2
starci git land <worktree> <ref> --dry-run --json
starci git land <worktree> <ref> --kernel-note "settle needs --evidence now"
```

### starci git sync

merge local main into a clean lane with rerere enabled

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--main-ref` | string (default main) |  |
| `--dry-run` | boolean |  |
| `--abort-on-conflict` | boolean |  |

Effect: local-write

Roles: lead, coordinator, owner

Conventions:

- lanes merge the LOCAL main, never origin/main
- the tracked worktree must be clean; untracked files are left alone
- rerere records conflict resolutions so the same resolution can be replayed

exit: 0 merged, already up to date or the dry run is clean; 1 dirty tree, conflict or Git failure; 2 invalid or remote-tracking main ref

json: starci/git-sync@1

```sh
starci git sync
starci git sync --dry-run
starci git sync --abort-on-conflict
```

### starci guard raw

apply command policy and run the real host tool behind a PATH wrapper

Positionals: program, arguments?

Effect: host

Roles: worker, lead, coordinator, release, owner

Conventions:

- the shared command policy decides every invocation before the real tool starts
- resolution skips the per-user StarCi shim directory so a wrapper never calls itself
- policy refusals exit 2; allowed commands return the real tool's exit code unchanged

exit: 0 the real tool succeeded; 2 command policy refused the invocation or usage was invalid; 127 the program was not found outside the StarCi shim directory

json: none

```sh
starci guard raw git -- status
```

### starci guard seat-tools

deny tools forbidden for the bound seat from JSON on stdin

exit: 0 hook decision emitted or the tool allowed (a malformed input is allowed too)

json: none

```sh
starci guard seat-tools
```

### starci guard verify-commit

verify a protected-branch update carries only worker-owned paths

Positionals: old, new

exit: 0 update allowed or the verifier failed open; 3 update refused because it carries foreign paths

json: none

```sh
starci guard verify-commit <old> <new>
```

## starci harness

start, stop, inspect or open the local StarCi harness

### starci harness open

open the local harness URL in the default browser

Effect: host

Roles: lead, coordinator, owner

Conventions:

- open uses the local harness URL derived from the runtime statusApp port

exit: 0 browser open requested; 1 the browser could not be opened; 2 bad usage

json: none

```sh
starci harness open
```

### starci harness start

start the harness API and UI or its named tunnel

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--tunnel` | boolean |  |

Effect: host

Roles: lead, coordinator, owner

Conventions:

- the API binds 127.0.0.1 at STARCI_STATUS_PORT when set, otherwise the runtime statusApp port
- the named tunnel reads %USERPROFILE%/.cloudflared/harness.yml and never accepts a token
- the local API stays in the verb process and Vite is its only child process

exit: 0 harness ran until stopped; 1 a harness child failed; 2 bad usage

json: none

```sh
starci harness start
starci harness start --tunnel
```

### starci harness status

report whether the harness health endpoint is up

Effect: read

Roles: worker, lead, coordinator, release, owner

Conventions:

- status probes /healthz at the local harness URL derived from the runtime statusApp port

exit: 0 harness is healthy; 1 harness is down or its probe failed; 2 bad usage

json: flag

```sh
starci harness status
starci harness status --json
```

### starci harness stop

stop only harness processes recorded by harness start

Effect: host

Roles: lead, coordinator, owner

Conventions:

- stop acts only when the recorded PID, creation time and harness start command all match
- a missing PID clears a stale record while an identity mismatch is retained and refused

exit: 0 recorded harness processes stopped or were already gone; 1 a recorded PID could not be verified or stopped; 2 bad usage

json: flag

```sh
starci harness stop
starci harness stop --json
```

## starci lint

lint exactly the files or repository scope named by the test ladder

### starci lint run

lint changed files or the release-scoped whole repository

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--level` | enum L0|L1|L2|L3|L4 (default L1) |  |
| `--changed` | list |  |
| `--all` | boolean |  |
| `--fix` | boolean |  |

Effect: read

Roles: worker, lead, coordinator, release, owner

Conventions:

- Use L1 while working, L2 before asking for a land, and L3 when an IO slot changed.
- L0 and L1 stay on changed files; L4 is the only whole-repository lint scope.
- Product apps go through starci app lint; the runtime uses its structural lint self-check family.

exit: 0 lint was clean; 1 lint findings; 2 usage or ladder policy refusal

json: starci/lint-run@1

```sh
starci lint run --level L1 --changed scripts/machine/ladder-lint.mjs
starci lint run --level L4 --all
```

## starci npm

install exact dependencies in one owned worktree under the host lock

### starci npm ci

install a clean lockfile into this worktree under the host lock

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--workspace` | list |  |

Effect: host

Roles: worker, lead, coordinator, release, owner

Conventions:

- npm ci installs the lockfile into this worktree's real node_modules and never uses a junction or symbolic link
- package.json and package-lock.json must be clean before the run
- dependency installs run one at a time under the host lock and never use npm install

exit: 0 the clean lockfile was installed; 1 npm or the host lock failed; 2 the worktree or install state was refused

json: starci/npm-ci@1

```sh
starci npm ci
starci npm ci --workspace packages/cli
```

add exact dependencies from canon pins under the host lock

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dev` | boolean |  |

Positionals: package

Effect: host

Roles: lead, owner

Conventions:

- bare package names resolve only from knowledge/hfs/canon-pins.yaml and never through a registry lookup
- explicit versions use exact x.y.z form and must agree with the canon pin when one exists
- installs always use --save-exact and report the package.json and package-lock.json diff stat

exit: 0 exact dependencies were installed; 1 npm, Git or the host lock failed; 2 the package or worktree was refused

json: starci/npm-install@1

```sh
starci npm install typescript
starci npm install left-pad@1.3.0 --dev
```

### starci release publish

plan or perform the owner-run package publication sequence

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--publish` | boolean |  |
| `--runtime-package` | boolean |  |
| `--npm-user` | string |  |
| `--poll-minutes` | number (default 15) |  |
| `--pre-land-ref` | string |  |
| `--expect-sha` | string |  |
| `--examples` | list |  |

Effect: publish

Roles: release, owner

Conventions:

- plan mode is read-only and reports registry blockers, canon rebind drift and example pin drift; the text and the json data.plan name every row and every blocker
- publication uses the existing clean proof, registry confirmation and integrity verification
- scripts/gates/release-plan.mjs publishOrder puts dependencies first and refuses cycles; packages without bundled canon pins win only among ready ties
- the package phase rebinds code patterns, re-pins and installs examples, syncs them and proves every binding
- runtime-package publishes root package.json after package publication, committed bindings and finished notes; it proves the real archive and private install
- runtime-package refuses changed inputs or registry state after its cold proof and never performs rebind or example writes
- publication never commits, pushes or tags; release cut owns those effects

exit: 0 plan is clear or publication completed; 1 a plan blocker, publication, rebind, example or binding step failed; 2 bad usage or environment

json: starci/release-publish-flow@1

```sh
starci release publish
starci release publish --publish --npm-user <name> --expect-sha <sha>
starci release publish --runtime-package --publish --npm-user <name> --expect-sha <sha>
```

Conventions:

- ordinary sync and check retain their existing copy behavior
- prepare-grammar installs and builds ignored grammar output and refreshes knowledge under the host lock before syncing copies
- check and prepare-grammar cannot be combined

exit: 0 copies were refreshed or already agree and requested grammar preparation passed; 1 copy drift, grammar preparation or host lock failure; 2 bad usage

json: starci/release-sync-runtime@1

```sh
starci release sync-runtime
starci release sync-runtime --check
starci release sync-runtime --prepare-grammar
```

## starci supabase

### starci supabase start

start the app's Supabase stack after enforcing its isolated port block

Effect: host

Roles: worker, lead, coordinator, owner

Conventions:

- one local Supabase stack belongs to one project and uses only its configured 41000-44999 port block
- never start a protected foreign stack or use ports 3000, 3100, 54320-54329 or 55321-55327
- secrets stay in sops and never appear in command output
- stop the project's stack when the work that needs it is done

exit: 0 the project stack started; 1 the Supabase CLI failed; 2 the config, port policy or host lock refused the start

json: starci/supabase-start@1

```sh
starci supabase start --cwd <app>
```

Roles: worker, lead, coordinator, release, owner

Conventions:

- status reads only the project rooted at supabase/config.toml and never a protected foreign stack
- secret key names may be listed but their values never appear in text or JSON

exit: 0 stack state was read including a stopped stack; 1 the Supabase CLI status read failed; 2 the app or project config was refused

json: starci/supabase-status@1

```sh
starci supabase status --cwd <app>
starci supabase status --cwd <app> --json
```

- secrets stay in sops and never appear in command output

## starci task

register and inspect the runtime's per-user Windows scheduled tasks

### starci task list

list state, runs, results and actions for registered runtime tasks

Effect: read

Roles: worker, lead, coordinator, release, owner

Conventions:

- only the runtime-owned harness app, harness tunnel and reconciler tasks are listed

exit: 0 registered runtime tasks listed; 1 Task Scheduler could not be read; 2 bad usage

json: starci/task-list@1

```sh
starci task list
starci task list --json
```

### starci task register

print or apply one runtime scheduled-task registration

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--apply` | boolean |  |

Positionals: name

Effect: host

Roles: lead, coordinator, owner

Conventions:

- without --apply the exact PowerShell registration is printed for review and no host state changes
- registration is idempotent, per-user and limited-privilege; it never needs administrator rights
- task actions invoke starci through the current user's .starci/bin shim (starci runtime link writes it)
- harness-app runs starci harness start; its Windows task name is statusApp.task of modules/models/runtimes.yaml, the name the reconciler restarts

exit: 0 registration printed or applied; 1 Task Scheduler registration failed; 2 bad usage or unknown task name

json: starci/task-register@1

```sh
starci task register harness-app
starci task register reconciler
starci task register harness-tunnel --apply --json
```

### starci task show

show state, runs, result and action for one runtime scheduled task

Positionals: name

Effect: read

Roles: worker, lead, coordinator, release, owner

Conventions:

- names select only the runtime-owned harness app, harness tunnel and reconciler tasks

exit: 0 task details listed; 1 Task Scheduler could not be read; 2 bad usage or unknown task name

json: starci/task-show@1

```sh
starci task show reconciler
starci task show harness-tunnel --json
```

## starci test

run the bounded L1-L4 test ladder without accidental whole-suite work

### starci test run

run the specs selected for one local ladder level

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--level` | enum L1|L2|L3|L4 | required |
| `--changed` | list |  |
| `--against` | string (default main) |  |
| `--spec` | list |  |
| `--concurrency` | number |  |
| `--root` | string |  |
| `--release-cut` | boolean |  |

Effect: host

Roles: worker, lead, coordinator, release, owner

Conventions:

- Use L1 while working, L2 before asking for a land, and L3 when an IO slot changed.
- Never run the whole suite outside L4; L4 belongs to starci release cut and L5 belongs to CI.
- L2 and L3 need a clean committed tree, run the full check first, and hold the one host test lock.
- A red L2 or L3 selection is re-run once serially; a green re-run is recorded as a flake, never skipped.
- File concurrency uses fresh idle CPU and free RAM under modules/supervisor/test-concurrency.yaml; --concurrency overrides it.
- The result and spec log retain the concurrency decision and host measurements.

exit: 0 selected specs passed; 1 a check or spec was red; 2 usage or ladder policy refusal

json: starci/test-run@1

```sh
starci test run --level L1 --changed scripts/machine/ladder-test.mjs
starci test run --level L2 --against main --json
starci test run --level L3 --against main
```

## starci typecheck

### starci typecheck run

check changed runtime modules or affected TypeScript projects

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--level` | enum L0|L1|L2|L3|L4 (default L1) |  |
| `--changed` | list |  |
| `--project` | list |  |

Effect: read

Roles: worker, lead, coordinator, release, owner

Conventions:

- Use L1 while working, L2 before asking for a land, and L3 when an IO slot changed.
- L1 checks projects holding changed files, L2 and L3 check affected projects, and L4 checks every project.
- Runtime JavaScript uses node --check; product TypeScript always uses tsc --noEmit through the Node API owner.

exit: 0 every selected program was clean; 1 syntax or type findings; 2 usage or ladder policy refusal

json: starci/typecheck-run@1

```sh
starci typecheck run --level L1 --changed packages/hfs/src/main.mjs
starci typecheck run --level L2 --project ui/tsconfig.json
```

## starci worker

start, inspect and completely close supervised Orca workers

### starci worker close

release a worker, close its terminal and prove its process tree is gone

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dispatch` | string | required |
| `--stop-first` | boolean |  |
| `--retry-release` | boolean |  |

Effect: host

Roles: lead, coordinator, owner

Conventions:

- always finish a worker with starci worker close; release alone is not complete cleanup
- --stop-first requires positive caller knowledge that the Dispatch is still working
- success requires release, terminal-close and process-exit proof

exit: 0 worker fully closed; 1 release, terminal-close or process-exit proof is missing; 2 bad usage

json: starci/worker-close@1

```sh
starci worker close --dispatch <dispatch-id>
starci worker close --dispatch <dispatch-id> --stop-first --retry-release
```

### starci worker list

list supervised workers or working-agent counts by worktree lane

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--run` | string |  |
| `--by-lane` | boolean |  |
| `--active` | boolean |  |
| `--worktree` | string |  |

Effect: read

Roles: worker, lead, coordinator, release, owner

Conventions:

- use --by-lane to see how many agents of each type work in each worktree

exit: 0 workers listed; 1 Orca data could not be read; 2 bad usage

json: starci/worker-list@1

```sh
starci worker list --active
starci worker list --by-lane
starci worker list --run <run-id> --worktree <path>
```

### starci worker read

read a bounded tail of one supervised worker's output

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dispatch` | string | required |
| `--lines` | number (default 80) |  |

Effect: read

Roles: worker, lead, coordinator, release, owner

Conventions:

- read by Dispatch id so Orca can use the exact transcript or its labelled terminal fallback

exit: 0 output read; 1 Orca could not read the worker; 2 bad usage

json: starci/worker-read@1

```sh
starci worker read --dispatch <dispatch-id>
starci worker read --dispatch <dispatch-id> --lines 200
```

### starci worker release

release settled Orca worker accounting without claiming full cleanup

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dispatch` | string | required |

Effect: host

Roles: lead, coordinator, owner

Conventions:

- release is retained for lifecycle recovery; normal completion always uses starci worker close
- release alone can leave an agent terminal and process running

exit: 0 worker released; 1 Orca could not prove the release; 2 bad usage

json: starci/worker-release@1

```sh
starci worker release --dispatch <dispatch-id>
```

### starci worker show

show one supervised worker and Orca's exact liveness observation

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dispatch` | string | required |

Effect: read

Roles: worker, lead, coordinator, release, owner

Conventions:

- address a worker by Dispatch id, never by its terminal title

exit: 0 worker shown; 1 Orca could not read the worker; 2 bad usage

json: starci/worker-show@1

```sh
starci worker show --dispatch <dispatch-id>
```

### starci worker start

start one supervised agent in a registered worktree in an Orca run

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--agent` | enum codex|claude|devin|cursor | required |
| `--model` | string |  |
| `--worktree` | string | required |
| `--spec` | string | required |
| `--task-title` | string | required |
| `--run` | string |  |

Effect: host

Roles: lead, coordinator, owner

Conventions:

- point the spec to a brief file; use @file only when its contents must be passed as the Task
- never pass --model for Devin; its account-selected model is not inferred
- stagger starts by about 30 seconds and assign one Codex worker to each disjoint chunk
- create the caller Run in this same terminal before starting its workers
- always finish the worker with starci worker close; release alone is not complete cleanup

exit: 0 worker started; 1 Orca or the host could not prove the start; 2 invalid agent, model, brief, worktree or Run binding

json: starci/worker-start@1

```sh
starci worker start --agent devin --worktree <path> --spec @brief.md --task-title "CLI worker verbs"
starci worker start --agent codex --model gpt-6.1-sol --worktree <path> --spec "Read briefs/worker.md" --task-title "Review worker verbs"
```

### starci worker stop

stop a supervised worker that Orca still reports as working

| flag | type | |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dispatch` | string | required |

Effect: host

Roles: lead, coordinator, owner

Conventions:

- stop only a working Dispatch; finish cleanup with starci worker close

exit: 0 worker stopped; 1 Orca could not prove the stop; 2 bad usage or the worker is not working

json: starci/worker-stop@1

```sh
starci worker stop --dispatch <dispatch-id>
```
